body.html: Lampang Vintage sits at 590 Moo 3, Thanon Prabaht, in the Ban Tok Hua Chang neighbourhood of Phrabat sub-district, Mueang Lampang. The thing guests mention most is that it's a simple edge-of-town stay with clean, roomy, quiet rooms, rice-field views, and it's very close to Lampang Airport. It's a small property of about 20 rooms, popular with people flying into Lampang who want somewhere near the airport, drivers stopping over for a night, or anyone after a clean, quiet room at a budget price — because from here it's only a short drive into the old town and Kad Kong Ta.

What guests agree on most is that the rooms are clean, roomy and great value. Many reviews say the rooms are cleaner than expected for the price, the beds are comfortable, the hot water works well, and the Wi-Fi is strong throughout the room. Rooms are air-conditioned with a flat-screen TV, a fridge/minibar, a private bathroom with shower, and some have a balcony looking out over rice fields and mountains. There are both Double rooms with a larger bed and Twin rooms with two beds. Guests say getting a clean, roomy, quiet room with breakfast at this price stands out for Lampang.
"Clean, roomy room, comfy bed, good hot water, strong Wi-Fi, quiet rice-field views, friendly staff, breakfast included — a few hundred baht and genuinely great value for Lampang."

Another thing guests like about Lampang Vintage is the quiet setting and the friendly staff. The property sits on the edge of town surrounded by rice fields, so it's quiet — good for anyone who actually wants to rest, with no street noise. There's an on-site restaurant, a garden and a terrace to sit out on. Breakfast is included in the rate, parking is free on-site, Wi-Fi is free, and the front desk is open 24 hours. Staff are a frequent highlight: many reviews say the team is friendly, speaks English, and is happy to suggest places to go and help with getting around.

The location needs to be said plainly, because it's both a plus and a limitation. It's on the edge of town in the Phrabat area, near the airport and the train station — very handy if you're flying or taking the train in — but it's not in the heart of the old town. From the hotel it's roughly a 10–15 minute drive into Kad Kong Ta and the old town, and you can carry on to Wat Phra That Lampang Luang. The upside is that it's quieter and parking is easy, but if you don't have your own car, heading out to walk the old town in the evening isn't convenient — you'll need to arrange a ride each time. The cool season (November–February) is Lampang's high season, rooms fill fast, so book ahead.

To be straight about it, this is a simple budget-level stay, not a full-facility hotel. The things that come up most in reviews: there's no swimming pool, some rooms are light on bathroom amenities, and a few reviews mention upkeep and a damp/musty smell in certain rooms. Some rooms don't have a kettle (there's coffee/tea in the lobby instead), and breakfast is simple — some guests would like more choice. Overall it's a place that delivers a clean, quiet room at a budget price rather than luxury or a full set of facilities.

All in, Lampang Vintage is about clean rooms, quiet, proximity to the airport and value, rather than an old-town walking base or a resort with a pool. It suits people with a car, or anyone flying or taking the train into Lampang who wants a clean, quiet stay near the airport at a few hundred baht with breakfast. If you want to sleep in the heart of the old town within walking distance of Kad Kong Ta, or you're after a riverside resort on the Wang with a pool, this isn't the answer. But if what you want is a clean, roomy room, a comfy bed, quiet rice-field views, strong Wi-Fi, easy parking and breakfast included at a budget price — it delivers that, and it's genuinely good value.

A tip from following the reviews here: if you want a nicer view, ask for a room facing the rice fields or with a balcony, and check at booking whether your room has a kettle if you need one. Because the location is on the edge of town outside the old quarter, it helps to have your own car or to plan on arranging a ride for evenings out at Kad Kong Ta. In the cool season book ahead, as it's high season, and always compare prices across platforms since breakfast-inclusive rates can differ.

You have to accept the edge-of-town setting that needs a car for the centre, no pool, and a few reviews about upkeep in certain rooms — in exchange for a clean, roomy, quiet room near the airport at a price that's hard to find in Lampang.

faq.q: Where is Lampang Vintage and what's nearby?
faq.a: Lampang Vintage is at 590 Moo 3, Thanon Prabaht, in the Ban Tok Hua Chang area of Phrabat sub-district, Mueang Lampang, on the edge of town surrounded by rice fields. It's about 3 km from Lampang Airport and close to the train station. It's roughly a 10–15 minute drive into Kad Kong Ta and the old town, and about 30 minutes on to Wat Phra That Lampang Luang.

faq.q: How much does Lampang Vintage cost and what room types are there?
faq.a: Rates start from approximately ฿550/night with breakfast for a Double room. They rise for the Twin room, the rice-field-view Double with a balcony, and a Family room. Cool-season rates (Nov–Feb) go up and rooms fill fast as it's Lampang's high season — always compare a few platforms before booking.

faq.q: Who is Lampang Vintage best for?
faq.a: It's ideal for people with a car, or anyone flying or taking the train into Lampang who wants a clean, quiet stay near the airport at a few hundred baht with breakfast. It works well as a one-night stopover or a base for exploring Lampang. It's less suited if you want an old-town walking location near Kad Kong Ta or a resort with a pool.

faq.q: What are the rooms and setting like at Lampang Vintage?
faq.a: The strengths are clean, roomy rooms, comfy beds, strong Wi-Fi, and a quiet setting with rice-field views. Rooms are air-conditioned with a flat-screen TV, fridge/minibar and a private bathroom with shower; some have a balcony. There's an on-site restaurant, garden, terrace and a 24-hour front desk, and the staff are friendly and speak English.

faq.q: What should I know before staying at Lampang Vintage?
faq.a: Things noted in reviews: it's on the edge of town outside the old quarter, so you need a car for the centre, and there's no pool. It's a simple budget stay, bathroom amenities are limited, and some rooms have no in-room kettle. A few reviews mention upkeep and a damp smell in certain rooms, and breakfast is simple.

faq.q: How far ahead should I book, and is cancellation free?
faq.a: In the cool season (November–February) book several weeks ahead, as it's Lampang's high season and the property has only 20 rooms, so they fill fast. Other times a few days ahead is fine. Every platform offers a Free Cancellation option — pick that if your plans aren't firm, and compare prices across platforms before booking.
